chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Harun ibn Mas'adah ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, 'In what is salvation tomorrow?' He said, 'Salvation is only in not deceiving Allah so that He deceives you. Surely whoever deceives Allah, Allah deceives him and removes faith from him, and he deceives himself.' It was said to him, 'How does a person deceive Allah?' He answered, 'He acts upon what Allah commanded, then intends by it someone other than Him.'

So fear Allah regarding show-off (riya'), for it is polytheism with Allah. Surely the one who does show-off will be called on the Day of Judgment with four names: O disbeliever, O mischief-monger, O cunning, O loser!
Your deeds are invalidated and your reward is nullified, so there is no escape for you today; go and seek your reward from the one for whom you were performing deeds.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of deceiving Allah and how does show-off lead to the nullification of deeds?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Thawab al-Amal, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies that deceiving Allah occurs when one performs obligatory acts with the intention of pleasing someone other than Allah, a condition known as *riya'* (show-off). This subtle form of polytheism (*shirk*) nullifies the reward of the deed, leading to the individual being called by four names on the Day of Judgment: *Kafir* (disbeliever), *Fajir* (mischief-monger), *Ghadir* (cunning), and *Khasir* (loser). The Prophet (s.a.w.s.) emphasizes that salvation lies in sincerity, warning that the reward for such deeds will be sought from the person for whom they were performed rather than from Allah.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his ancestors that the  Holy  Prophet  (s.a.w.s.)  was  asked,  “What  will  have salvation  on  the  Day  of  Judgment?”  The  Holy  Prophet (s.a.w.s.) replied, “Salvation is only and only in not cheating Allah so that He also doesn’t cheat you. Surely Allah cheats a person who cheats Him and takes faith away from him. A person should know that he has cheated himself.” The Holy Prophet  (s.a.w.s.)  was  asked,  “How  does  a  person  cheat Allah?” He answered, “By obeying the order of Allah but for the sake of someone else.

Keep away from showoff because it is polytheism. Surely, a person who does showoff will be called  with  four  names  on  the  Day  of  Judgment  viz.  O disbeliever, O mischief-monger, O cunning, O loser!
Your deeds are wasted. Your reward was reduced continuously and there is nothing left for you today. Go and ask for the reward from one for whom you performed good deeds.”
